races.name: Faucets The Bathroom Specialists Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Birthday Boy Leighton Happy 80th Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Coffee Pod
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Muir & Grassick whose sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 runs is a significant concern; Ryan Kavanagh takes the 3lb claim but this horse rarely threatens at the business end of races over 5f on Good.

runners_data.name: Miracleoftheandes
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Warren Greatrex with Jack Callan up; has placed on Good ground over 5f and will look to dominate from stall one, but recent form trail shows vulnerability when pressed throughout.

runners_data.name: Portacloy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the Kublers with Daniel Muscutt aboard; tongue-tie fitted, 21-day break, and sim-going record of 1 placing from 7 runs suggests modest but genuine claims for a horse likely to be well-placed throughout behind the speed.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Headgear-flagged prominent/hold-up type with a genuine win on Good over 5f and three further placings from 15 sim-going runs; Laura Coughlan's claim helps in the weights and this horse's tactical flexibility on fast ground makes it dangerous in several race shapes.

runners_data.name: Sheik Yerbouti
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a clear fade-in-finish flag and 57 days off the track for Grace Harris; sim-going record of just 1 run in similar conditions and a limited recent form string of 803 all point to a horse likely to set the pace but fail to sustain it.

runners_data.name: Little Jaybee
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a fade flag for David Evans; J F Egan takes the ride but recent form — 9th twice at this trip on Good — is unencouraging, and this 3-year-old has never troubled the judge in 5f contests on Good or Soft.

runners_data.name: Happier
runners_data.note: Trainer Martin Keighley has fired one from two in the last 14 days, but this horse is in truth a hold-up performer squeezed into the midfield projection because the pace map is full at the rear — its chance is tempered by the likelihood it cannot secure a truly restful position in a contested-pace race.

runners_data.name: River Edge
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f specialist for Christopher Mason with a solid placing record (2W2P from 6 sim-going runs) who operates off the pace; the map shows midfield because genuine hold-up horses outnumber available rear slots — Gina Mangan will look to drop in and produce a late effort if the straight opens up.

runners_data.name: Miss Gold
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old for David Flood stepping back sharply in class (OR 45) but carrying a fade flag and a sim-going record of 0 wins from 4 runs; also a true hold-up type shown in midfield due to field congestion at the rear, making her chance in this fast-run race particularly slim.

races.paceDynamic: Miracleoftheandes and Sheik Yerbouti are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this sharp 5f at Ffos Las, ensuring an honest, pressured gallop from flag to finish on Good ground. Sheik Yerbouti carries a fade-in-finish flag and is likely to give way inside the final furlong, while Miracleoftheandes has the stronger recent form at this trip and going combination and should dictate the shape. The contested pace will burn off the leaders late and play into the hands of horses able to race prominently off a strong gallop — specifically Portacloy, who sits just behind the speed, and Dark Sun, whose Good-ground form over 5-6f is the strongest in the field. Three runners — Happier, River Edge, and Miss Gold — are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more horses wanting to race off the pace than positions allow; in reality this race will be run too fast up front for any of them to truly get cover and produce a late run from an ideal position, with Happier and River Edge the most likely to attempt something from off the pace if gaps appear. This race shape — pressured front two, honest gallop, flat 5f — strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the early duel who can pick up the pieces in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Miracleoftheandes and Sheik Yerbouti fight it out early and the pace is strong enough to leave both flat late.
scenarios.body: The contested lead sets a genuine tempo that drains the front two, leaving a prominent horse travelling just behind to swoop through in the final furlong; Good ground at Ffos Las over 5f consistently rewards this profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Sustains, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Miracleoftheandes gets a clear advantage and the pace is strong but controlled enough to allow a brief breather mid-race.
scenarios.body: With Sheik Yerbouti fading and no horse able to close from deep, Miracleoftheandes converts its early lead into a front-running victory; its two-from-four placing record on Good going supports a bold-running effort at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that the field strings out and gaps open late in the straight for a closer to pick through.
scenarios.body: Happier or River Edge, the two most capable hold-up performers here, benefit if chaos in the straight creates a clear passage; River Edge's consistent 5f Good-ground form (four placings from six runs in similar conditions) makes it the most likely beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Sheik Yerbouti and Miracleoftheandes race too freely early and tie up, causing the whole field to bunch and produce a messy finish.
scenarios.body: A scrambled, compressed run-in over the final furlong advantages a horse with residual energy racing mid-to-prominent, particularly those with a strong finishing kick at this course configuration; Dark Sun's pace adaptability over 5f on Good gives it the edge in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Sheik Yerbouti's fade flag combined with 57 days off track means watch for it weakening sharply inside the final 2f, potentially causing traffic issues for horses immediately behind as the field compresses.

Miracleoftheandes (stall position unknown) and Sheik Yerbouti may jostle aggressively for the early lead — if both are drawn wide relative to each other, an early crossing move could unsettle horses immediately behind at the 4f pole.

River Edge has run over 5f on Good ground six times and placed twice but is likely to find itself unable to produce its natural hold-up run cleanly if the field doesn't string out; watch for Gina Mangan switching wide late.

Dark Sun's headgear and recent Good-ground form (1W3P from 9 sim-going runs) makes it a key horse to track from the half-mile pole — if it is travelling comfortably at that point it is well-placed to exploit a fading front two.
The Coffee Pod has not won or placed on Good ground in 15 comparable runs — if it is prominent early it may be doing so under pressure rather than by choice, signalling the pace is genuinely strong.

races.name: Meyer Timber EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Dandara Homes Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Nammos
runners_data.note: The key pace-setter for this race; Carson knows him well and will likely control the tempo uncontested, but his sim-going record of 0W0P on similar ground and a style-fit flag suggest he may be flattered by an easy lead rather than being a genuine winner.

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact trip on Good ground (1/8f/GOO) and has previous form on similar surfaces — the most compelling form angle in the field, with the 3lb claim of Ryan Kavanagh a minor offset; true hold-up style suits a contested gallop better than a slow one.

runners_data.name: Kev
runners_data.note: An 85-day absence is a significant query, and his recent form string (0-0980) alongside a warning flag for finishing fade and just one placing from eight starts on similar going make him very hard to support here.

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: John & Thys Flint run Nammos too, so stable tactics are worth monitoring; Rival has placed three times from seven runs on similar going and is best suited to sitting just off the pace — a controlled Nammos gallop is exactly what he wants.

runners_data.name: Oviedo
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true style sees him at the back, though redistribution has him shown in midfield; the fade flag and a sequence of 9-9-10-10-9 recent finishes at various trips makes his chance remote regardless of race shape.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Showed a third and a second in recent Good-ground miles and has a headgear angle (p); a 7-day turnaround is sharp but connections run him regularly — his REDISTRIBUTED status means he is a natural closer who may be forced forward, which could actually suit if the pace is slow.

runners_data.name: Uncle Albert
runners_data.note: Headgear (t) fitted, but a string of finishes between 6th and 9th across soft and good ground over the past five runs, plus a fade flag, makes it very difficult to make a case — genuinely needs a fast pace to have any chance of reaching the frame.

runners_data.name: Change Of Fortune
runners_data.note: Drops back from 10-12f trips to a mile here, and has only one comparable run on similar going from 15 attempts — the step down in distance and poor recent form (9th last time) are both concerns despite the prominent placing at 12f on soft.

runners_data.name: Ivat Ghia
runners_data.note: A young 3-year-old who placed second over this exact trip on Good ground in his most recent similar-going run (2/8f/GOO); Tyler Heard takes the ride, headgear (h) is in place, and he has shown enough to be competitive if the race develops into a genuine contest.

runners_data.name: Big Moonrise
runners_data.note: Returning from a 197-day absence and steps up from 7f to a mile, which is unexplored territory; only three career runs to his name and the redistribution maps him into midfield though his true instinct is to come from off the pace — the layoff and lack of mile form make him a big unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Nammos is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner mile handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to pressurise him, William Carson should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a frantic early burn. Rival is the only other horse mapped as prominent, meaning the front two are likely to set a steady-to-fair tempo with a largely strung-out field behind them. The majority of this field — Angel's Call, Kev, Oviedo, King Of The Dance, Uncle Albert, Change Of Fortune, Ivat Ghia and Big Moonrise — are all natural hold-up or rear-of-field types, but with so many genuine closers entered, several of them (most notably King Of The Dance and Ivat Ghia, who have shown ability to race prominently) will be forced wider or further forward than they'd like, creating a compacted midfield rather than a true trailing group. A controlled lead for Nammos, uncontested and allowed to control the pace from the front, means prominent racers or horses with tactical speed to pick off a modest gallop are best placed, while the crowded hold-up brigade face a genuinely awkward scenario where they must produce sustained runs from a position that isn't truly their own.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nammos Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Nammos dictates an unchallenged, measured gallop and the pace is just honest enough to suit those travelling prominently.
scenarios.body: Nammos sets the fractions without pressure, Carson can regulate the tempo to suit himself, and Rival or any horse able to sit just off the pace will get first run into the straight with energy to spare. A steady-to-fair gallop at a mile on Good turf rewards the horse with tactical speed and a clean passage, not the deep closers who need a genuine end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns out to be genuinely honest and the hold-up horses find gaps in the straight, negating the front-runner's advantage.
scenarios.body: Nammos and Rival do enough to force a true gallop, and one of the genuine hold-up horses — Angel's Call, who won last time out at this trip on Good ground, or Ivat Ghia, who placed at this distance on Good — produces a sustained late run to collar the leaders close home. This scenario requires clean passage for the closer through what will be a congested midfield, making it harder to execute given how many horses are racing out of their natural position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Nammos goes too slow and the compressed midfield surges collectively, turning the straight into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A dawdling early gallop causes the large hold-up contingent to bunch up behind the leader well before the turn, effectively erasing any advantage and creating a flat-out dash in the final two furlongs. Horses with a higher cruising speed from a prominent position benefit most in this lottery-style finish, but the congestion penalises any horse needing a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Pacesetter Disrupts
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected horse — most likely King Of The Dance or Ivat Ghia — pushes forward and challenges Nammos for the lead, forcing a contested gallop.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested pace at a mile on Good ground raises the tempo considerably, stretching the field and potentially burning out the nominal front-runner before the straight. In this race shape the advantage shifts to the horse who is quickest to recover their balance after a fast-run mile, but given most hold-up types here are racing out of role, few are ideally set up to exploit it.

watchPoints.text: Nammos and Rival are trained by the same yard (John & Rhys Flint) — watch for stable tactics; if Carson on Nammos is instructed to ensure a true gallop to set it up for Rival, the race shape changes significantly.

King Of The Dance, despite being a natural hold-up horse redistributed to midfield, has recent Good-ground mile placings and could push forward if his jockey senses the pace is too slow — monitor his early position as a potential pace disruptor.

Angel's Call is the standout form angle on paper having won last time over this trip on Good, but her true hold-up style means she needs gaps to appear in the straight — a bunched midfield could cost her momentum at the crucial moment.

Big Moonrise returns from 197 days off and steps up in trip — watch market moves in the final hour as any significant support for an unexposed 3-year-old with J F Egan in the saddle could indicate stable confidence behind the scenes.

The going is Good throughout the card at Ffos Las with no deterioration reported — conditions are consistent and unlikely to favour any particular horse on ground-specific grounds, keeping the race shape as the primary differentiator.

races.name: Golwg Gwendraeth "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Flat Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Port Louis
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with course-distance experience, but recent form reads 208038 and it fades in the finish; its true hold-up style means it will be shuffled away from the rear in this field and asked to race in a position that does not suit it naturally.

runners_data.name: Next Guilian
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Rod Millman's stable who has placed twice on Good ground in three similar-going starts; races as a hold-up type but with only three career runs is still lightly exposed and could progress past its current OR of 70.

runners_data.name: The Stone Power
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett-trained three-year-old who is the only confirmed front-runner here and will enjoy an uncontested lead; a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 notes it is mapped slightly out of role, but as the race's sole pace-setter it is the key tactical reference point for the entire field.

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old holds form figures of 4-6-3-8-2 including two places on Good ground; 54 days off the track is a minor query but Daniel Muscutt takes the ride and its naturally handy style suits a pace shape built around a lone front-runner.

runners_data.name: John Harrison
runners_data.note: Alan King's three-year-old has placed in three of its last five, including back-to-back thirds on Good ground, and is handled by claimer Luke Catton (3lb); it is a true hold-up horse pressed into a midfield berth by the race's composition, which tempers confidence in it executing its finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Brave New World
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has run three times, all at seven furlongs, all for seventh or worse; stepping up to a mile is logical but the form book offers nothing encouraging, and like the other hold-up types it will be unable to settle as far back as it would ideally want.

races.paceDynamic: The Stone Power is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field dominated by hold-up types, meaning it will stride to the front unchallenged and control a relaxed, sustainable gallop over this flat Ffos Las mile on Good ground. With no rival willing or able to press it early, the pace is likely to be honest but not strong, creating a race that sets up for those tracking in behind rather than those needing a truly searching tempo to peel off the back. Port Louis, John Harrison, and Brave New World are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to a midfield mapping because the field cannot accommodate that many closers; in reality, several must race closer to the pace than they would prefer, which dilutes the effectiveness of the hold-up profile. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader dictating an even tempo — most favours horses that can sit prominently or in mid-division tracking the pace and quicken off a steady gallop, with Royal Bodyguard and Next Guilian best positioned to exploit the pace structure without racing out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stone Power Controls, Tracking Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If The Stone Power leads at a fair but uncontested gallop and the closers lack the kick to reel it in.
scenarios.body: The Stone Power dictates from the front without pressure, setting a metronomic pace that rewards horses who sit within two or three lengths and pick it off in the closing stages; Royal Bodyguard, with a handy recent third on Good, is ideally suited to track and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stone Power Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses are unable to close the gap when the pace is too slow and The Stone Power simply stays on.
scenarios.body: A very gentle early gallop means The Stone Power never faces pressure and its rivals lack the sprint to reel it back; the front-runner converts its tactical advantage into an outright win on the steady surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Find Gap Late
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up horses — Port Louis or John Harrison — manage to find a clear run and the pace is strong enough to set up a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Despite racing out of their natural role, either Port Louis or John Harrison could benefit if a burst of mid-race pressure quickens the tempo and creates gaps inside the final furlong; both carry form on Good ground at this trip but their redistribution significantly reduces the likelihood of executing their optimal style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Inexperienced Three-Year-Olds Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the lightly-raced three-year-olds like Brave New World or Next Guilian outrun their form figures on the day.
scenarios.body: Brave New World and Next Guilian are unexposed at the mile trip and could improve sharply beyond their bare form if the steady pace suits developing stamina; however, Brave New World's three career runs all produced seventh-place finishes and the form line is thin.

watchPoints.text: The Stone Power's ability to control the pace completely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if it bowls along at a comfortable clip, watch whether Royal Bodyguard can track it closely enough to strike in the final two furlongs.

Port Louis, John Harrison, and Brave New World are all natural hold-up horses who cannot all settle at the rear in a six-runner field; watch for early shuffling and potential interference as multiple horses are forced wider or closer than intended.

Royal Bodyguard returns after 54 days off the track for Michael Bell — watch the market moves and how it moves through the race, as a flat handler with one win from 22 over 14 days is a moderate booking angle.

The going is confirmed Good throughout the Ffos Las card with no significant variation reported at the mile trip, meaning no runner receives an unexpected surface advantage — watch for any early morning dew that could marginally ease conditions.

Both three-pound claimers — Luke Catton on John Harrison and Ashley Lewis on Brave New World — reduce weight but add positional risk; watch whether either horse is left without daylight in a small field with multiple out-of-role runners.

races.name: Dress For The Occasions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Meet Me In Meraki
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer for David Evans, J F Egan takes the ride with the stable in reasonable form (1 from 14 over 14 days); best form on Good going and the 12f trip suits, but the sim-going strike rate (3 places, 0 wins from 15) is modest and the horse will need a tactical collapse to get competitive from deep.|

runners_data.name: Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied and wearing a hood, Bernard Llewellyn's six-year-old has placed at 12f on Good ground which is the one encouraging note here; the sim-going record shows only 1 win and 3 places from 15 attempts suggesting consistency without dominance, and the 29-day break after a modest 3rd is fine but no booster.|

runners_data.name: Noble Grace
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's five-year-old holds a recent win at 12f on Good ground and is genuinely in form (4741 recent string), but as a true hold-up runner operating in a field with too many closers, the horse is shoe-horned into midfield rather than the rear where it wants to be — the style-fit discount (0.91) is real, and Ashley Lewis takes an apprentice claim that may assist.|

runners_data.name: Belle Of Kt
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: J S Moore's five-year-old has won twice recently (1m2f-1m4f) and is the only horse here with confirmed front-running credentials; Millie Wonnacott (5lb claimer) makes the weight competitive, and the drop in OR to 54 means she gets in light — her Good-ground sim record (0 wins, 1 place from 15) is the one note of caution but she sets this race up entirely.|

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: David Flood's lightly-framed three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — three wins in recent form but a dramatic 14th last time out on Good at 12f introduces significant questions about consistency; the 8-day turnaround is quick and, while the sim-going record (3W, 5P from 14) looks strong, those wins came on a different pace shape than the one presented here.|

runners_data.name: Claytons Kolatonic
runners_data.note: This three-year-old drops into the map's midfield despite being a natural closer, having run exclusively at 7f-8f in its recent form — the step to 1m4f is a huge stamina question and the 58-day absence adds uncertainty; Jack Doughty takes the ride for Dominic Ffrench Davis (no wins from 3 over 14 days), and the entire chance hinges on an untested stamina reserve.|

races.paceDynamic: Belle Of Kt is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously challenge her for the lead, she is set to control the pace entirely on her own terms over this 1m4f on Good ground at Ffos Las. Racing from the front uncontested, she can regulate fractions to suit herself, which historically favours the leader at this track and distance when the pace is genuinely moderate. The hold-up contingent — Noble Grace, A Daughters Love, and Claytons Kolatonic — are all true closers but are redistricted into midfield on the race map because the rear is overcrowded with the same profile, meaning they will not all settle where they naturally want to be. This shape overwhelmingly favours the prominent racer who can dictate and control, with any closer needing a genuine injection of pace in the straight to generate the momentum to reel in a settled front-runner on good ground — a scenario that looks structurally unlikely here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belle Of Kt Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Of Kt jumps cleanly and is allowed to set a comfortable, measured pace throughout with no rival willing to pressure her.
scenarios.body: Belle Of Kt dictates every fraction on this flat track, finds a rhythm that suits her proven front-running form (two recent wins), and has enough in reserve to kick clear in the straight; her jockey Millie Wonnacott can manage the race entirely from the front, giving nothing away.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp A Fading Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Of Kt's early pace is unsustainably fast or she begins to tie up from the 2f pole, opening the door for hold-up types to reel her in.
scenarios.body: A Daughters Love or Noble Grace, both genuine closers shuffled into midfield but retaining their late-run instincts, could pick up the pieces if the leader empties out; the good ground does not penalise them, and either has the form to capitalise on a fading front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to soften the leader but the closers from deep struggle to sustain their run over 1m4f on this flat track.
scenarios.body: Meet Me In Meraki, operating from hold-up but on a course and distance profile that suits a switch to a closer-prominent role, times a run to arrive at the right moment; Bulldog Spirit, who has placed at the trip on Good ground, could emerge as the one genuine each-way threat from the chasing pack if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Pace Map
scenarios.trigger: If there is a traffic incident, a slow early pace causes a bunched sprint finish, or multiple horses contest the lead unexpectedly.
scenarios.body: If closers redistribute themselves further forward than anticipated, the race shape collapses into a flat-out sprint from 2f out, which could suit a horse with a sharp turn of foot on the day regardless of style classification; Claytons Kolatonic, stepping up sharply in trip and carrying unexposed stamina, would be the biggest beneficiary of an unusual pace collapse.

watchPoints.text: Watch Belle Of Kt's early stride and whether Millie Wonnacott allows her to bowl along or tries to restrain — if she is ridden aggressively from the front, the race is likely run and won from the front before the final bend.

A Daughters Love's previous 14th on Good at 12f is unexplained and the 8-day turnaround is sharp for a three-year-old — if that run signals a physical problem rather than a tactical mishap, her chances evaporate on pedigree grounds alone.

Claytons Kolatonic has never raced beyond 8f and takes a near-doubling of trip today — watch in the parade ring for any signs of restlessness or in-running for the horse dropping away quickly after 1m, which would confirm the stamina ceiling.

Noble Grace's apprentice jockey Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) changes the weight dynamics slightly and could allow the horse to travel more comfortably in the early stages; if Lewis manages to slot Noble Grace closer than its natural position, the race shape could tighten marginally.

The going is consistently Good across all distances at Ffos Las today including this 1m4f — no advantage from contrasting underfoot conditions and no late-draw bias concern on this flat, left-handed course.
